main_text.p: tis explorata dogmata, manus conferere cogitate cujus sit artis, anguillas illas lubricas et cœno gaudentes, sed quid ego anguillas dico? apage deminutiva; quin angues potius [Greek: μεταμορφωμένους] (Sectarios, inquam, & sophistas) e cavis et limo quibus se abdiderunt eruere, in lucem protrahere, ita constrictos tenere, neque aut toxico noceant, aut elabantur lubrico. Cogitate quanta sit folertia, latentem sub ovilla veste lupum deprehendere; Detrahere & pellem nitidus qua quisque per ora Cederet introrsum. turpis: hypocritarum & Enthusiastarum, qui obtentu Reformationis orbi illudunt, qui sub larva Spiritus carni militant, qui libertatem prophetandi sibi arrogant ut aliis licentius imponant, quid sibi velint & quo tendant occulta consilia sapienter perspicere, eorumque conatibus tempestive & prudenter obvenire, [Greek: τίς πρὸς τοῦτο]; Quotu quisque est ea natura

page.notes: The Greek words in the line "angues potius" and "τίς πρὸς τοῦτο" are badly damaged and only approximately read; the Greek "μεταμορφωμένους" reading is uncertain. The word "Quotu'quisque" is underlined in the print. The final word "riium" is printed at the right margin as "rium"; read as "riium"/"rium" with uncertainty. The left strip of cut-off text is the neighbouring page's margin and is not transcribed.
